figures.caption: \textbf{(a)} Schematic of interaction energies. Variation of the van der Waals frequency shift $V(R_{ij})=C_6/R_{ij}^{6}$ (blue) with interatomic distance $R_{ij}$ for the ground state $|ggg\rangle$, single-excited state $|W_1\rangle$, doubly excited state $|W_2\rangle$, and excited state $|rrr\rangle$. \textbf{(b)} Neutral atom layout with separated storage and computation regions. The figure shows a three-atom support set $S_3=\{q_1,q_2,q_3\}$ ($\theta_{S_3}$, blue) and a five-atom support set $S_5=\{q_4,\dots,q_8\}$ ($\theta_{S_5}$, green). \textbf{(c)} In the degree-graded basis, the M\"obius matrix $M=\zeta^{-1}=\mu_1^{\otimes n}$ takes a block lower-triangular form with identity diagonal blocks $I_{(k)}$ of size $\binom{n}{k}$.
figures.label: fig:native_mobius_overview

figures.caption: The M\"obius Compiler for Atoms pipeline. A diagonal algorithm is Möbius-inverted into projector hyperedges, synthesized as native occupation-projector gates or decomposed (Layer 1), ASAP-scheduled (Layer 2), routed on the storage/entanglement-zoned architecture (Layer 3), and verified bit-exactly (Layer 4). The M\"obius-native and ZAP-decomposed strategies differ only at the synthesis step and share the scheduler, router, and fidelity model.
figures.label: fig:moca_pipeline

figures.caption: Circuit decomposition comparison for the same compact 6-qubit 3-SAT oracle instance. Panels (a)--(c) show the original ZAP decomposition, the ZX no-insert-calculus decomposition, and the M\"obius-native decomposition, respectively. ZAP lowers the M\"obius projector terms to one- and two-qubit gates, ZX extracts a different no-insertion phase circuit from the standard input circuit, and the M\"obius-native path keeps the occupation-projector supports as native phase gates. In the drawing, single-qubit phases with angle $\pm\pi/4$ are displayed as $T$ and $T^\dagger$ gates, RZ angles in panel (b) are shown modulo $2\pi$ for compactness, and projector phases are displayed as $Z$ gates or filled-dot controlled-phase symbols whose dots mark the participating qubit lines and whose labels give the phase angle $P(\theta)$. Each logical CNOT in the ZAP template is expanded as $H$--$CZ$--$H$ to match a CZ-native neutral-atom gate set. The respective displayed depths and gate counts are $128/163$, $37/64$, and $12/19$. The displayed ZX no-insert circuit contains one $CCZ$ block, while the M\"obius-native circuit retains six $CCZ$ blocks. The two terminal SWAP gates in panel (b) are the output-wire permutation returned by the ZX extractor; they are retained and counted here so that all three circuits act on the same fixed qubit ordering.
figures.label: fig:sat3_circuit_comparison

figures.caption: Performance comparison for eight common algorithmic benchmark families. Each panel plots routed total fidelity on a logarithmic scale versus qubit count for the M\"obius-native compiler, the original ZAP decomposed baseline, and the ZX no-insert-calculus baseline. The first six panels are Hamiltonian or oracle benchmarks with explicit many-body interaction terms, where native multiqubit execution can reduce decomposed gate exposure and scheduled stages. The last two panels are two-body controls, where the three compilation paths are expected to be similar.
figures.label: fig:eight_panel_fidelity

figures.caption: Atom-movement comparison for eight common algorithmic benchmark families. Each panel plots the number of routed atom move events versus qubit count under the partitioned architecture model and compilation strategies used in Fig.~\ref{fig:eight_panel_fidelity}. Because native multiqubit blocks execute in the shared entanglement zone, this metric reports the transport overhead paid to gather gate supports across storage partitions.
figures.label: fig:eight_panel_moves

figures.caption: Representative runtime-scaling comparison for three many-body/oracle algorithm families from 20 to 100 qubits. The top row plots total routed circuit duration versus system size, and the bottom row plots the corresponding total classical compile time, including decomposition or synthesis together with neutral-atom scheduling and routing. Each panel compares the M\"obius-native compiler, the original ZAP decomposition, and the ZX no-insert-calculus baseline on the same storage-partitioned architecture.
figures.label: fig:duration_compile_scaling

figures.caption: Native-gate error sensitivity for routed 30-qubit benchmark instances. The columns are 3-SAT, p-spin Ising, and QRAM; the top row compares M\"obius-native against ZX no-insert, and the bottom row compares M\"obius-native against the original ZAP decomposition. The color shows $\Delta F=F_{\rm M}-F_{\rm B}$, where $F_{\rm B}$ is the row-specific baseline, while routed movement, idle, transfer, and one-/two-qubit gate parameters are fixed. The solid black curve is the break-even boundary, the dashed vertical line marks a $p_4$-independent boundary, and the star marks the representative native-gate table used in the benchmark. The 3-SAT column has only three-body native exposure, so the boundary degenerates to a vertical line; p-spin Ising and QRAM show genuine two-parameter sensitivity.
figures.label: fig:native_error_phase_diagrams

figures.caption: Scheduled-stage comparison for eight common algorithmic benchmark families. Each panel plots the routed ASAP scheduled stage count versus qubit count for the benchmark families and compilation strategies used in Figs.~\ref{fig:eight_panel_fidelity} and~\ref{fig:eight_panel_moves}. The first six panels contain explicit many-body Hamiltonian or oracle terms and expose the stage reduction available from native multiqubit execution. The last two panels are two-body controls where the M\"obius-native and original ZAP paths largely coincide.
figures.label: fig:eight_panel_stages

figures.caption: Auxiliary ZX insert circuit for the same compact 6-qubit 3-SAT oracle instance used in Fig.~\ref{fig:sat3_circuit_comparison}. The circuit is drawn with the same gate notation as Fig.~\ref{fig:sat3_circuit_comparison}: filled dots mark the participating qubit lines of controlled phase gates, $P(\pi)$ two-body phases are displayed as CZ-type controlled phases, three-body $P(\pi)$ phases are displayed as CCZ-type controlled phases, and RZ angles are shown in parentheses next to the RZ gate. For this instance the displayed ZX insert circuit has depth $32$ and $45$ displayed gates, including six displayed $CCZ$ blocks, whereas the main-text ZX no-insert panel has displayed depth $37$ and $64$ displayed gates with one displayed $CCZ$ block.
figures.label: fig:sat3_circuit_comparison_zx_insert
